data.title: J&J/Contineum depression candidate fails in phase 2
data.description:
• An asset for major depressive disorder licensed to Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) from Contineum Therapeutics (CTNM) missed its primary endpoint in a phase 2 trial.
  • In the MOONLIGHT-1 trial, JNJ-5120/PIPE-307 did not improve the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) total score compared with placebo. 
  • J&J will continue to evaluate the data to determine next steps. 
  • JNJ-5120, an M1 muscarinic receptor antagonist, also failed a phase 2 trial for relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis in November 2025.

data.title: dLocals taps Oscilar to boost compliance workflows across 60+ markets
data.description:
• dLocal (DLO) announced on Monday that it has selected Oscilar to strengthen its compliance operations across 60+ markets and 1K+ payment methods.
  • Oscilar will support AML monitoring, sanctions screening, and investigations, with workflows tailored to different markets.
  • Its AI agents will help compliance teams review alerts and handle time-consuming tasks while human analysts keep final control over decisions.
  • The move is aimed at helping dLocal manage rising payment volumes and changing regulatory requirements without adding the same level of operational complexity.
  • Oscilar also provides audit trails and explainable decisions, giving dLocal greater visibility and control over its compliance processes.

data.title: Leidos wins $875M U.S. Navy contract option
data.description:
• The U.S. Navy awarded Leidos (LDOS) an $875M second option year under the Next Generation Enterprise Network Service Management, Integration and Transport contract.
  • Leidos will support more than 650,000 Navy and Marine Corps personnel and manage over 425,000 devices across 2,500+ global sites.
  • The company will provide user support, network operations and IT transformation services across NMCI, ONE-Net and MCEN networks.

data.title: Tesoro Minerals upsizes private placement to C$1M
data.description:

data.title: Walmart's ad business stands out as high margin contributor—Goldman Sachs
data.description:
Walmart’s (WMT) U.S. advertising business, Walmart Connect, is contributing more to the company’s operating income than sales thanks to the ad business’ 70% margin and 40% year-over-year growth in the past few quarters, said Goldman Sachs analyst Kate McShane following a discussion with management at Goldman’s Communacopia & Technology Conference.

With Walmart (WMT) roughly 6 years into its advertising journey, its success in effective customer reach, investment in customer attention, ease of spending for customers, and a clear return on investment component “enables the company to outperform the majority of other retailers while maintaining a lighter ad load than many of its peers.”

The company’s VIZIO acquisition transformed its connected TV capabilities. Last year, this partnership enabled Walmart audience targeting and measurement across VIZIO inventory, and 2026 marks the first full year those capabilities have been available to Walmart (WMT) Connect advertisers.

In the first half of this year, the VIZIO OS was the number one smart TV operating system in the U.S. And last month, Walmart (WMT) completed its Vibe.co acquisition, a self-service streaming TV advertising platform that complements Walmart’s existing business by providing a gateway for small and mid-sized businesses.

In conclusion, McShane believes Walmart’s (WMT) advertising business is "highly profitable" and will continue to benefit from e-commerce growth.

“Management explained that the growth of e-commerce and advertising have a direct relationship given that the more Walmart customers are addressable online, the bigger the advertising business will be, which leads to higher e-commerce gross merchandise value,” McShane writes.

data.title: Dave & Buster's swings to a loss on negative comp sales, higher operating costs
data.description:
Higher food and beverage, payroll, and pre-opening costs eroded Dave & Buster’s (PLAY) profitability in the second quarter, driving the company into the red and underperforming Wall Street’s expectations.

Shares were underwater in after-hours trading, reflecting the disappointing financial results and negative comparable store sales.

The restaurant chain swung to an unexpected adjusted loss of $0.27 per share versus a profit of $0.40 per share a year ago, missing expectations for a profit of $0.19 per share. Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $98.9M from $129.8M in the same quarter last year, missing $118.8M estiamtes. .

Sales experienced a more modest decline of 2.4% year-over-year to $544.1M but were still less than anticipated as comparable store sales were down from a year ago. 

The results reflected lower entertainment revenue and increased food and beverage revenue, while at the same time, expenses increased across most of its items, with food and beverage costs up 11%, entertainment costs up 5%, and payroll costs up 1%. As a result, total operating expenses increased by 4%.

Dave & Buster’s (PLAY) balance sheet improved, however, generating positive adjusted free cash flow of $19.5M for the first six months of 2026 compared to negative $36.5M for the same period last year.

data.title: Veracyte acquiring Convergent Genomics in up to $180M deal
data.description:
• Veracyte (VCYT) has agreed to buy Convergent Genomics, which is focused on urologic cancer diagnostics, for $150M upfront.
  • The acquisition gives Veracyte, which provides cancer genomic tests, access to Convergent's UroAmp MRD, a urine test that can detect, monitor, and predict the risk of urothelial cancer or its recurrence well before signs and symptoms develop or become detectable.
  • So far, UroAmp MRD has been validated in non-muscle invasive bladder cancer.
  • Convergent could receive another $30M in milestone payments based on UroAmp reimbursement efforts.
  • Veracyte said it plans to expand use of UroAmp to other indications, such as intravesical maintenance therapy monitoring and surveillance following treatment with curative intent.
